definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese storehouse with thick earthen walls designed to be fireproof and protect valuables, foodstuffs, and heirlooms. A distinctive feature of traditional Japanese architecture.

examples.japanese: この{町|まち}には{古|ふる}い{土蔵|どぞう}が{残|のこ}っている。
examples.english: Old earthen storehouses remain in this town.

examples.japanese: {土蔵|どぞう}の{中|なか}から{江戸|えど}{時代|じだい}の{絵|え}が{見|み}つかった。
examples.english: A painting from the Edo period was found inside the storehouse.

examples.japanese: {土蔵|どぞう}の{厚|あつ}い{壁|かべ}は{火事|かじ}から{中|なか}の{品物|しなもの}を{守|まも}る{役割|やくわり}を{果|は}たした。
examples.english: The thick walls of the earthen storehouse served to protect the goods inside from fire.

notes:
USAGE:
{土蔵|どぞう} refers specifically to a storehouse with thick walls made of earth and plaster. They are typically white-walled and can still be seen in historic towns and merchant districts across Japan. Many have been converted into cafes, galleries, or shops.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土蔵|どぞう}{造|づく}り (storehouse-style construction)
- {白壁|しろかべ}の{土蔵|どぞう} (white-walled storehouse)
- {土蔵|どぞう}を{改装|かいそう}する (to renovate a storehouse)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {蔵|くら}: storehouse, warehouse (general term)
- {倉庫|そうこ}: warehouse (modern, commercial)
